outcome: The general conjecture remains open, but several papers since 26 January 2024 settled Vaught's conjecture for further restricted classes of theories: countable complete theories with a definable infinite discrete linear order (Tanović, arXiv:2212.13605 v3, March 2024), theories of partial orders admitting a finite lexicographic decomposition and unions of products of rooted trees (Kurilić, arXiv:2601.03155 and arXiv:2606.12014, 2026), and the omega-Vaught's-conjecture for Ehrenfeucht theories via a Scott-analysis framework (arXiv:2606.15205, 2026).

disputes.summary: Robin Knight has announced (2002, 2007) a purported counterexample to Vaught's conjecture and the topological Vaught conjecture; as of the most recent secondary sources found (through 2021, and no update located in the 2024-2026 window), it has not been verified or published in a form the community accepts. No new development on this dispute was found within the window, so it does not change the status here, but it is the single most consequential open thread on this problem and is noted for completeness.

summary: I treated this as the general first-order Vaught conjecture (finite/ℵ₀/2^ℵ₀ trichotomy for countable models of a countable complete theory), per the statement given, and searched for anything that changed the state of that conjecture since 26 January 2024. Nothing resolved or refuted the conjecture itself. Several genuine partial results (cases of the conjecture, in the §3.1 sense of restricting rather than varying the question) appeared in the window: (1) arXiv:2212.13605 (Tanović), 'Vaught's conjecture for theories of discretely ordered structures' — v1 predates the frozen revision (Dec 2022) but v3, dated 24 March 2024, is the version that proves the final result (continuum-many countable models for any countable complete theory with a definable infinite discrete linear order); I date the event to the v3 posting since that is the first written form of the completed argument, per §6.3's rule to use the first written argument. (2) Miloš Kurilić's 2026 papers on partial orders admitting a finite lexicographic decomposition (arXiv:2601.03155) and unions of products of rooted trees (arXiv:2606.12014), each proving VC for those specific classes. (3) arXiv:2606.15205, 'Scott Analysis below the Vaught Ordinal', which proves the ω-Vaught's-conjecture (a known strengthening/variant, not identical to the classical conjecture) for Ehrenfeucht theories — this is arguably a 'related problem' under §3.1 rather than a strict case, since the ω-VC is a different statement, though it specializes to VC-relevant consequences for that class; I lean toward counting it as informative context rather than the primary basis for 'partial' status, and rest that status mainly on the Tanović and Kurilić results, which are unambiguous cases. I read the arXiv:2508.06854 Pillay–Tanović item as a survey, not a new result. None of these papers mention any AI system, machine learning, automated theorem proving, or Lean/Coq formalization anywhere I could check (abstracts, and for the two I could render as text, fuller content); all are traditional human-authored proofs in the classical style of this literature, which has a decades-long tradition of chipping away at VC one class of theories at a time. I also checked for any AI-related developments on Vaught's conjecture generally (searches for AI-assisted proofs, Lean formalizations, DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository) and found nothing connecting any AI system to this problem in any way. The long-outstanding Robin Knight counterexample claim (2002/2007) remains, as far as I could determine, unverified, with no update found in the window; I recorded it as a dispute rather than letting it drive the status, since nothing changed about it during the window.
competing_reading: One could argue that arXiv:2606.15205's ω-Vaught's-conjecture result is a 'related problem' (a different, stated variant) rather than a case of the classical conjecture named in the Wikipedia bullet, in which case it should be excluded from the basis for 'partial' and only cited in summary as related. This would not change the overall status, since the Tanović and Kurilić results independently establish 'partial' on their own as clear cases (restrictions to specific theory classes) of the exact statement in the bullet.
what_would_settle_it: A full resolution of the ℵ₁-model case under ¬CH (the one case Morley's theorem leaves open), or verification/refutation of Robin Knight's long-standing counterexample claim, would settle the general conjecture. Absent that, the question of whether the ω-Vaught's-conjecture result should count as a case versus a variant would be settled by a closer reading of how the ω-VC modifies the hypotheses of the classical statement.

I also did not exhaustively check every possible AI-assisted-mathematics announcement venue (e.g., individual lab blogs) for an unpublicized claim about Vaught's conjecture, relying instead on targeted searches that turned up nothing; given how narrow and traditional this subfield is, and the total absence of any AI mention across every paper I could open, I am reasonably but not fully confident nothing was missed.

judgement.doubts: F7: the record dates Tanović to v3 (24 March 2024), but v1 is December 2022 and the record gives no evidence that v3 adds new mathematics beyond calling it 'the version that proves the final result'; it may be a pre-snapshot event. Status does not depend on it: the two Kurilić 2026 case results are clearly post-snapshot. The event field still points at Tanović v3; a reader should treat Kurilić 2601.03155 as the safer basis. The omega-VC result is a variant and does not count.
